title: T30-R1 source-state impact and object-lifetime assessment

scope.focus: T30-R1 late DBINDER_INCREFS relation after server-side socket close

source_binding.method: Downloaded immutable raw.githubusercontent.com URLs at target commit; recomputed SHA-256 and Git blob IDs over exact bytes.

source_state_graph.route: DatabusSocketListener::OnBytesReceived -> DBinderDatabusInvoker::OnMessageAvailable -> StartProcessLoop -> worker queue -> JoinProcessThread/OnTransaction -> DBinderBaseInvoker::ProcessTransaction
evidence: databus_socket_listener.cpp:124-135 obtains the current-thread DBinder invoker and forwards bytes.
dbinder_databus_invoker.cpp:333-360 validates framing and calls StartProcessLoop.
dbinder_base_invoker_interface.h:383-419 queues ThreadProcessInfo to an idle data worker.
dbinder_databus_invoker.cpp:458-475 drains the queue and invokes OnTransaction.
source_state_graph.result: Transaction processing is deferred to worker thread(s); source does not prove SoftBus shutdown callback thread identity or callback ordering.

source_state_graph.route: ProcessTransaction -> CheckAndSetCallerInfo -> QueryAppInfoToStubIndex(AppAuthInfo) -> TargetStubSendRequest -> QueryStubByIndex(cookie) -> SendRequest
evidence: dbinder_databus_invoker.cpp:808-839 derives pid/uid/device/token from the current session, checks the tuple/stubIndex/socket relation, then sets caller info.
ipc_process_skeleton.cpp:1656-1675 accepts a map row only when socketId is 0 or equals the current socket.
dbinder_base_invoker_process.h:43-80 takes objectMutex_, obtains a raw pointer from QueryStubByIndex, then calls SendRequest; it does not acquire an sptr/strong ref for the duration.
source_state_graph.result: A request can pass authorization before close and later reach the handler if already queued; a close before QueryStubByIndex instead makes lookup return null once the stub index is erased.

source_state_graph.route: ServerOnShutdown -> OnDatabusSessionServerSideClosed -> StubDetachDBinderSession -> DetachAppAuthInfoBySocketId -> QueryStubByIndex -> DecStrongRef
evidence: databus_socket_listener.cpp:89-100 dispatches shutdown through IPCThreadSkeleton::GetRemoteInvoker on the callback thread.
dbinder_databus_invoker.cpp:655-676 removes socket-bound relations, then looks up each surviving stub index and drops one strong ref.
ipc_process_skeleton.cpp:1598-1631 erases matching socket rows under appAuthMutex_ and returns their indices.
ipc_thread_skeleton.cpp:123-148 stores IPCThreadSkeleton in pthread TLS; GetRemoteInvoker (204-240) returns that current thread's invoker.
dbinder_base_invoker_define.h:171 stores objectMutex_ on each invoker instance; dbinder_base_invoker_interface.h:245-248 returns that member.
source_state_graph.result: The mutex used by close and TargetStubSendRequest is per invoker, and invokers are selected from thread-local skeletons; the source does not establish cross-thread mutual exclusion.

evidence: ipc_object_stub.cpp:232-263 reads caller tuple from the already-gated invoker, queries this stub's index, and calls AttachOrUpdateAppAuthInfo with stub=nullptr.
ipc_process_skeleton.cpp:1489-1516 inserts or replaces the tuple/stubIndex/socket row, then returns false immediately for stub==nullptr.

IPCObjectStub increments the strong ref only on successful bootstrap/ConnectRemoteObject2Session AttachOrUpdate calls with a non-null stub (ipc_object_stub.cpp:646-650; dbinder_databus_invoker.cpp:927-953), not in the INCREFS handler.
source_state_graph.result: If close removes the row after the request passed the gate, the delayed INCREFS can reinsert a row for the closed socket without acquiring a matching strong ref.

source_state_graph.route: last strong ref -> IPCObjectStub::OnLastStrongRef -> DetachObject -> EraseStubIndex -> DetachAppAuthInfoByStub
evidence: ipc_object_stub.cpp:489-502 removes the stub index and calls DetachAppAuthInfoByStub on last strong ref.
ipc_process_skeleton.cpp:994-1009 QueryStubByIndex returns a raw pointer under a shared lock; 1044-1057 removes the index; 1576-1596 erases authorization rows for that index.
source_state_graph.result: If close's decrement destroys the object, the subsequent late INCREFS cannot execute safely unless it already obtained the raw pointer; if it did already obtain the raw pointer, the per-invoker lock mismatch leaves a conditional use-after-free window. If the object remains alive, its eventual teardown removes the stale row.

active_app_auth_consumer_family: AttachOrUpdateAppAuthInfo: writes tuple/stubIndex/socket and optionally commAuth_ (ipc_process_skeleton.cpp:1489-1534).
DetachAppAuthInfo: exact tuple/stubIndex/socket erase; if successful, also removes matching CommAuthInfo (1536-1574).
DetachAppAuthInfoByStub: removes all rows for a stub index and matching CommAuthInfo (1576-1596).
DetachAppAuthInfoBySocketId: close cleanup removes socket rows and socket-bound CommAuthInfo, returns stub indices (1598-1632).
consumer_inventory.legacy_app_info_api_family: The same field is also accessed by Attach/Detach/QueryAppInfoToStubIndex overloads at ipc_process_skeleton.cpp:1069-1239 using appInfoToIndexMutex_, while the appAuth family uses appAuthMutex_. The inspected production source call sites use the AppAuthInfo family; no call from production sources to the legacy overloads was found. Treat the dual-lock arrangement as an API maintenance hazard, not an established concurrent race on the live B/IPC route without a production caller.
stub_index_to_object_consumers: TargetStubSendRequest uses raw lookup and SendRequest within invoker objectMutex_ (dbinder_base_invoker_process.h:43-80).
close uses raw lookup and DecStrongRef within GetObjectMutex (dbinder_databus_invoker.cpp:655-676).
IPCObjectStub::OnLastStrongRef erases index and relation state (ipc_object_stub.cpp:489-502).

late_relation_alone.authorization: The late row is bound to a closed socket ID; close removes that socket DBinderSessionObject. It cannot independently authorize a future session: a new server-side bind separately requires QueryCommAuthInfo, and stub=nullptr does not create CommAuthInfo.
late_relation_alone.strong_reference: No IncStrongRef occurs in DBinderIncRefsTransaction. The stale row does not itself pin the object.
late_relation_alone.leak_or_stale_state: If the object remains alive through unrelated holders, the stale row can persist until a later relation update or object teardown. It is a bounded row for an existing tuple/stubIndex, not an unbounded per-request allocation. Last-strong-ref cleanup removes it by stubIndex.
late_relation_alone.over_decrement: No direct extra decrement occurs at the stale-row write. A later socket close would drop one reference for any row it removes, but reconnect requires separate CommAuth authorization and relation rebinding; source does not establish a reachable path in which this stale row alone yields an unmatched decrement.

separate_raw_pointer_window.condition: A worker has passed CheckAndSetCallerInfo and QueryStubByIndex returned the raw stub pointer; a concurrently running close callback removes the relation and its DecStrongRef reaches zero before/during SendRequest.
separate_raw_pointer_window.source_mechanism: TargetStubSendRequest and close use objectMutex_ on invokers obtained from thread-local IPCThreadSkeleton instances. The worker queue is a distinct thread route, and no strong temporary reference is acquired after raw QueryStubByIndex.
separate_raw_pointer_window.possible_effect: Conditional use-after-free/premature destruction while SendRequest is executing, if the closed peer's relation is the last strong ref and SoftBus invokes shutdown concurrently with worker dispatch.
limits: Whether SoftBus callback timing actually overlaps the worker route is not established by IPC source alone.
If close wins before QueryStubByIndex, lookup fails after OnLastStrongRef erases the index; that ordering is fail-closed.
The in-flight raw-pointer window is related to the race but is not caused by the late stale row; do not infer it solely from stub=nullptr.

impact_verdict.second_layer_candidate: Retain exactly one low-confidence conditional candidate for independent product/runtime review: concurrent shutdown may destroy a stub after raw QueryStubByIndex and before/during SendRequest. The late INCREFS map row is only secondary state and is not the vulnerability mechanism.
impact_verdict.title: Cross-thread socket close can release the last stub ref while a queued request holds a raw stub pointer
impact_verdict.primary_mechanism: After CheckAndSetCallerInfo succeeds, TargetStubSendRequest can QueryStubByIndex and obtain a raw IRemoteObject*. A server-side shutdown callback on another thread-local invoker can remove the same socket relation and DecStrongRef the object to zero before or during SendRequest. Per-instance objectMutex_ does not serialize the two threads, and the request path does not acquire a temporary strong reference.

test_feedback.t32_reference: T32 feasibility result received from lead: gate-success barrier -> socket close detach/ref drop -> late INCREFS -> observe mapping/refcount delta is a suitable deterministic test design.
blockers: No OHOS clang/sysroot or generated args.gn/build.ninja available in this environment.
The local IPC/SoftBus checkout is not paired to target IPC commit bbb92dbb2f52aca54ab268307c9476ac1802f3ff/product build.
required_next_evidence: Build the target-paired IPC test binary and pause after TargetStubSendRequest has QueryStubByIndex returned the raw pointer but before SendRequest; concurrently close the socket and observe last-ref/destructor/index state.
Run control schedule with close before raw lookup (expected null/fail closed), and the race schedule with close after raw lookup but before/during SendRequest.

Separately observe the late INCREFS mapping after close; verify it cannot bind/authorize a new socket absent CommAuthInfo and whether a valid independently authenticated rebind repairs/reuses the row without reference imbalance.

summary.disposition: The primary conditional candidate is a raw-pointer lifetime race across thread-local invoker locks, subject to SoftBus overlap and last-reference runtime conditions. Late INCREFS creates a no-ref stale relation but is not itself an authorization bypass or proven ref leak. Retain one candidate for target-paired D32 verification; do not confirm vulnerability.
